fields.description: Enable Seerr integration for all users. Moonfin handles authentication through a server-side proxy so users can sign in once and stay authenticated across clients.
fields.label: Enable Seerr

fields.description: Where Silo can reach your Seerr server. Start the address with http:// or https://. Examples: http://192.168.1.10:5055 (another machine on your network) http://seerr:5055 (Docker, on the same network as Silo) https://requests.example.com (a public address) This is the address the Silo server connects to behind the scenes, not the one you open in a web browser, so a local network or Docker address works fine. You do not enter a username, password, or API key here; people sign in later from the app. Advanced: If a reverse proxy in front of Seerr shows its own login page, let the Silo server through it. If Silo itself sits behind a reverse proxy, make sure that proxy forwards /Moonfin/ requests to Silo.
fields.label: Seerr URL

fields.description: Optional override. The name shown in the UI (e.g., "Requests", "Media Requests"). Leave blank to auto-detect from the configured URL. The icon is always auto-detected regardless of this setting.
fields.label: Display Name (Optional)

fields.description: The address Seerr uses to reach this Silo server for request notifications (the webhook Seerr calls back). Set this when Seerr and Silo run in separate containers or hosts, since the server otherwise can only guess a local address that Seerr may not be able to reach. Use the base URL, for example http://192.168.1.10:8090 or https://silo.example.com. Re-provision webhook
fields.label: Public Server URL (Optional)

fields.description: Hosted relay that forwards push to backgrounded clients. Leave the default unless you run your own relay. Used only when no service account below is configured.
fields.label: Push Relay URL (Optional)

fields.description: Override the built-in relay key. Most self-hosters leave this blank. This is a secret and is never logged.
fields.label: Push Relay Key (Optional)
fields.placeholder: Leave blank to use the built-in key

fields.description: Paste the Firebase service-account JSON to enable push notifications so backgrounded or closed mobile clients still receive request updates. Generate it in the Firebase console under Project Settings → Service accounts. This is a secret and is stored in the plugin config. Leave blank to disable push.
fields.label: Push Service Account (Optional)
fields.placeholder: Paste the Firebase service-account JSON here

fields.description: Optional path to the service-account JSON file on the server. When set, it takes priority over the pasted JSON above.
fields.label: Push Service Account File Path (Optional)

fields.description: Nightly task that matches your anime against AnimeFillerList so Moonfin clients can badge filler episodes. No account or API key is needed. Series are matched by title, falling back to the English and romaji titles behind their ids for libraries in other languages, and only shows the site actually lists are fetched.
fields.label: Classify anime episodes as canon, mixed or filler

fields.description: Affects the Subbed/Dubbed pills. Normally an item also has to look like anime on its own, meaning it carries an AniList, AniDB, AniSearch, Kitsu or MyAnimeList id, or an "Anime" genre or tag. That check is what keeps a library holding both anime and ordinary shows from marking the ordinary ones. If the libraries you picked above are only anime, turn this on: the check then only costs you the entries whose metadata happens to be thin, which would otherwise show no pill at all. Has no effect while no libraries are selected, since there is then nothing to trust.
fields.label: Treat everything in the selected libraries as anime

fields.description: AnimeFillerList has no recap category, so this asks MyAnimeList as well. It is best-effort and additive: if that lookup fails, the filler data is unaffected.
fields.label: Also mark recap episodes (uses MyAnimeList)

fields.description: Reads the audio tracks in each file: Japanese and nothing else is Subbed, anything carrying another spoken language is Dubbed. A season gets a pill only when every episode in it agrees. This needs no internet and does not depend on AnimeFillerList, so it works for anime the site has never listed. Files whose audio has no language tag are left unmarked rather than guessed at. In a mixed library: when you select your anime libraries above, only shows in them are marked. If you leave the selection empty the whole server is in scope, and a series is then only marked when it looks like anime on its own, meaning it carries an AniList, AniDB, AniSearch, Kitsu or MyAnimeList id, or an "Anime" genre or tag. A Japanese live-action show carrying one of those would still be marked.
fields.label: Also mark episodes and seasons as Subbed or Dubbed

fields.description: Extends the same audio rules to movies, so the pill shows on a movie card anywhere it appears, including home screen rows. Separate from the option above because a movie has no series to inherit from, and a mixed library is most likely to mislabel a film.
fields.label: Also mark movies as Subbed or Dubbed

fields.description: A file holding the Japanese audio and a dub can be watched either way, so it shows as Subbed/Dubbed rather than just Dubbed. Leave off for the shorter label.
fields.label: Label dual-audio files as Subbed/Dubbed

fields.description: Applies to episode rows in Moonfin clients. Season and movie cards always draw the pill over the artwork, since they have no runtime line to sit next to.
fields.label: Where to put the pills

fields.description: Shows older than this are re-fetched (default 30). A finished show's classifications never change, so this mainly governs how quickly an airing show picks up new episodes.
fields.label: Marker refresh age (days)

fields.description: Records every marker request a client makes and what it was answered with, to moonfin-anime-markers.log in the server's own log folder, so it also shows up under Dashboard > Logs where it can be downloaded. Turn this on when a badge is not appearing: if a request never shows up here, the app never asked, which means the problem is in the app rather than on the server. Leave it off otherwise.
fields.label: Write a marker debug log

description: Not available on Silo, because Silo doesn't let plugins read its library. These settings are saved but do nothing. The library picker is on the Moonbase page.
title: Anime Filler & Recap Markers

fields.description: Lets Moonfin clients browse and play ROMs from a "Mixed Content" library using EmulatorJS. Organize ROMs as System/<game>/rom.ext with any BIOS files at the top of each system folder. No setup is needed for the emulator itself: cores stream from the EmulatorJS CDN by default. For offline use, drop the EmulatorJS data/ folder into <plugin data>/emulatorjs/data/ and it is used automatically.
fields.label: Enable retro games

fields.description: PSP games need cross-origin isolation to start in Moonfin Web, and the player only gets it when the whole app is isolated. Turn this on if PSP games stop with an error, then reload Moonfin Web. Once it's on, anything cross-origin you've added to the web client has to allow isolation too.
fields.label: Isolate the web app for PSP games

description: Not available on Silo, because Silo doesn't let plugins read game files. These settings are saved but do nothing. The core upload and library picker are on the Moonbase page.
